Hi Lena — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers and proposed next steps: 

1) Invoice recipient / remit: Yes — we can route invoices to Novamed Holdings, Inc. and send PDFs to procurement@novamed.com. To implement we need:
   - Legal entity name and tax ID (W-9 or equivalent) for the US remit entity.
   - Billing contact name/phone for AP escalation.

2) VAT / tax handling: We have two common patterns we use in the Order Form appendix:
   A) Seller-responsible for VAT language (Redwood remits VAT where required) — simplifies customer accounting but increases gross price in regions with VAT.
   B) Buyer-responsible (buyer pays VAT/gross-up) — keeps base price stable; customer handles reclaim where applicable.

Given your tax team's preference for buyer-responsible language, option B is feasible. We'll need to: 
   - Add a short clause in Appendix 2 (Taxes) clarifying that all applicable VAT/GST is payable by the customer and that any reverse-charge treatment or evidence collection obligations will be documented in Exhibit A (tax evidence checklist).

3) Minimum commit phasing / invoicing cadence: Quarterly true-ups are possible for the minimum commit, but we need to preserve Redwood's cashflow protections. Proposal: quarterly invoices for minimum commitment with mid-quarter usage estimates; at quarter-end we do a reconciliation invoice (true-up) that settles any shortfall/overage. This will require:
   - Order Form table updated to show commit cadence = Quarterly and invoice frequency = Quarterly (with monthly usage reports).
   - An activation clause that defines when the quarterly period starts.

Next steps I propose:
   - If you can share the US tax ID / W-9 and AP contact today, I'll update the Order Form and Appendix and circulate a tracked PDF to legal.
   - Ben and I will loop Legal (Kimberly) if the MSA needs an appendix amendment vs. a purely Order Form insertion.

I can have a redline out by Wednesday EOD PT if you can confirm the remit entity details.

Cheers,
Nikhil Sharma
Account Executive, Americas
Redwood Inference
